source.title: Mirror Descent Maximizes Generalized Margin and Can Be Implemented Efficiently
source.authors: Haoyuan Sun; Kwangjun Ahn; Christos Thrampoulidis; Navid Azizan

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper changes the optimizer geometry and measures test accuracy and model properties, testing whether implicit regularization choices affect generalization in overparameterized networks. This is a conceptual test of the claim's optimizer and measured-property themes, not of random-label memorization or most listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-10 and ImageNet generalization results for p-GD variants and weight-histogram measurements. It does not test the cited random-label, width, architecture-comparison, adaptive-optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example claims. The linear classifier norm tables measure implicit bias but not a version's named generalization outcome.
record.test_reason: The study measures how p-GD geometry affects image-classifier accuracy and weight distributions, but none of V1–V8 names that comparison. In particular, p-GD versus SGD does not test V4's adaptive-optimizer comparison, and weight histograms do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. The record's tests/T2 classification should be corrected.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, the authors prove directional convergence of p-GD for separable linear classification to an existing regularized direction with sufficiently small steps; for exponential-tail losses this is the corresponding p-norm maximum-margin direction. Deep-network experiments show changes in weight structure and held-out accuracy, without proving the linear characterization extends to those networks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses p-GD variants on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet to study implicit regularization and held-out accuracy; does not reproduce the original studies' interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported CIFAR-10 and ImageNet held-out accuracies vary with p; p = 3 gives the highest reported accuracy among tested p values in each listed network.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing p changes held-out accuracy. On CIFAR-10, p = 3 achieves the highest reported mean for all four architectures; on ImageNet, it achieves the highest accuracy for both architectures in single trials.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The geometry of p-GD affects image-classifier generalization under a shared training recipe, with p = 3 best among the tested values in these experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet-18 weight distributions concentrate more strongly near zero at p = 1.1; maximum absolute weights are 5.126, 1.393, 1.083 and 1.062 for p = 1.1, 2, 3 and 10 respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing p-GD geometry changes learned weight distributions and maximum absolute weights in CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 models.

record.problems: ImageNet experiments used one trial and models did not reach 100% training accuracy; the authors state the models were outside the interpolation regime and that not using weight decay cost around 3% validation accuracy in the p = 2 case. The CIFAR-10 runs report five-trial standard deviations. Linear experiments use randomly generated separable data and do not measure generalization.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Linear-classifier norm results are omitted because they concern norm minimization and implicit bias, not outcomes measured by a claim version.

untested.parts: No paired random-label and natural-label training and held-out comparisons; natural-label interpolation alone does not establish coexistence.
No width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or intervention on local connectivity.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison, broader tuning comparison, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching experiment.
No batch-size comparison under fixed or extended epoch budgets.
No dropout intervention or joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
No magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, correlation with generalization gaps, or ranking against norm and margin measures.
No removal and retraining comparison involving memorized versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded numerical values match the supplied source. Table 6 additionally reports CIFAR-10 results for p = 1.5 and p = 6, despite the record's assertion that no rows were left out; these results also fit no listed version. The ImageNet weight-decay observation does not test V6's dropout or joint-removal comparison. No version-specific missing results or verdicts are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation threshold and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and tuning conditions.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and its effect on test accuracy.
